title: Holiday Baking Pantry Stock-Up: How to Organize Baking Supplies Before Cookie Season
description: Three half-open bags of flour and no baking soda? Organize your baking supplies before cookie season, plus 8 Amazon finds for an easy baking pantry.
intro:
Holiday baking starts with a hopeful plan and usually ends with a mid-recipe discovery: we're out of eggs, there are three open bags of powdered sugar, and the vanilla is nowhere.

Baking is extra hard for our brains because it needs a lot of small things at the same time. If one is missing, the whole thing stops, and it's hard to start again.

So before cookie season really kicks off, let's give baking supplies one home, make it easy to see what's running low, and stock up on purpose. Here's the plan, in small steps, plus eight Amazon finds that make the baking pantry easier.

sections.heading: Step 1: Gather it all in one spot (10 minutes)
sections.body:
Baking stuff tends to live everywhere: flour in the pantry, sprinkles in a drawer, cookie cutters in the back of a cabinet. Pull it all onto the counter or table.

Toss anything expired. Combine duplicates. You might find you already own four bags of chocolate chips. (We've all been there.)

sections.heading: Step 2: Make a baking zone
sections.body:
Pick one shelf, cabinet or bin and make it the baking zone. Everything for baking lives there and only there.

A turntable or a few clear bins work great, so you can see everything at once. If your pantry is tiny, use a single big bin you can slide out and put on the counter.

sections.heading: Step 3: Decant the big four
sections.body:
Flour, sugar, brown sugar and powdered sugar get used the most and spill the most. Moving them into clear, airtight containers makes it easy to scoop, easy to see how much is left and much less messy.

Label each one on the front. Flour and powdered sugar look a lot alike at 9 p.m.

sections.heading: Step 4: Group the little things
sections.body:
Sprinkles, food coloring, extracts and baking powder are small and easy to lose. Put them together in one small bin. Same for cookie cutters, piping tips and cupcake liners.

Now "where's the vanilla?" has one answer: the little-things bin.

sections.heading: Step 5: Write a stock-up list from what you see
sections.body:
With everything in view, it's easy to see what's missing. Write a short stock-up list now, before the baking starts:

- Flour, sugars, butter, eggs
- Baking soda and baking powder (check the dates)
- Vanilla and any extracts
- Chocolate chips and sprinkles
- Parchment paper or baking mats

Take a photo of your list so it's on your phone at the store.

sections.heading: Step 6: Keep a 'running low' note on the door
sections.body: Stick a small notepad or dry-erase board inside the pantry door. When you open the last bag of something, write it down right then. Your grocery list builds itself while you bake.

finds.why: Big clear containers with a wide opening, so you can scoop and see how much is left at a glance.

finds.name: Clear pantry bins with handles

finds.why: Slide the whole baking bin out to the counter, bake, then slide it back. One home for everything.

finds.name: Pantry turntable
finds.why: Spin to find extracts and food coloring instead of knocking over everything in front.

finds.name: Pantry label maker or labels
finds.why: Flour and powdered sugar look the same. A label on the front ends the guessing.

finds.name: Silicone baking mats

finds.why: Reusable, so one less thing to run out of mid-recipe. Cookies slide right off.

outro:
A baking pantry that works for our brains is one home, see-through containers and a list that writes itself. Set it up once and cookie season gets a lot more fun.

If the rest of the kitchen could use a reset too, *The Messy Brain Home Reset* walks through it one small zone at a time.
